metadata.title: AI Product Failure Lab
metadata.voice_note: Synthetic local Kokoro voice reading Aditya's script in first person (disclosed in SOURCES.md).
metadata.bookend_exempt_reason: Course pitch film (INFO7375 final project pitch, 2–4 min): opens on the hesitant writer + terms card, no verdict card, and no Your Turn beat, which would spend runtime on a viewer exercise instead of the seven required pitch answers. The spoken outro stays.
metadata.audience: INFO7375 instructor and TAs; hiring managers for AI product manager roles
metadata.honesty: Past tense only for the idea, the blueprint doc and the baseline tests. Drawings of the unbuilt product are tagged 'constructed'.

skin_warnings: BIDEA: palette=claude but the cold open is 'BrutalistHesitantWriter' — COLD OPEN LAW wants ClaudeComposerAsk

beats.narration_text: Hi, I'm Aditya Hasija. Every product starts with one question: will it work? I think the more useful question is how it will fail.
beats.motion_claim: The writer types the hopeful question and corrects it to the useful one: how will it fail.

qc.sparse_reason: Hesitant-writer bookend: the correction is the motion.

beats.narration_text: Two terms. A pre-mortem: you imagine the product has already failed, and ask why. And an evaluator: an agent that checks the other agents' work.

shot.visual_intent: Left: a cracked idea crate with a question mark rising from it (pre-mortem). Right: a review desk where a page lands under a lamp (evaluator). One label each.
shot.motion_claim: Left: a cracked idea crate with a question mark rising from it (pre-mortem). Right: a review desk where a page lands under a lamp (evaluator). One label each.

beats.narration_text: Most ideas don't fail on day one. They fail months later, on an assumption nobody checked. I want to catch that assumption before anyone builds.

shot.visual_intent: A kraft idea box drops onto the stage. Its lid lifts and three pages rise; one page's outline turns terracotta and a crack line draws across it.
shot.motion_claim: A kraft idea box drops onto the stage. Its lid lifts and three pages rise; one page's outline turns terracotta and a crack line draws across it.

beats.narration_text: I'm proposing the AI Product Failure Lab. A product manager gives it an idea and public sources, and it will return a pre-mortem: five failure risks, every claim labelled, and three tests to run first.

shot.visual_intent: The idea box and a source binder slide into a dark machine block; three report pages slide out on the other side, one after another.
shot.motion_claim: The idea box and a source binder slide into a dark machine block; three report pages slide out on the other side, one after another.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn object or scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, voice carries the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: It will live in a GitHub repository: a small web app, a test set of made-up product ideas, and a log that scores it.

shot.visual_intent: A release parcel opens; a browser window, a fan of test cards and a log page rise out of it.
shot.motion_claim: A release parcel opens; a browser window, a fan of test cards and a log page rise out of it.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn object or scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, voice carries the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: Inside, an orchestrator will pass the idea to market, customer and risk agents. An evaluator will challenge what they found, and can send one back once. One retry, never a loop.

shot.visual_intent: A junction routes the idea packet to three dark agent blocks; their pages travel to a review desk under a lamp; one page goes back to one block exactly once, then returns.
shot.motion_claim: A junction routes the idea packet to three dark agent blocks; their pages travel to a review desk under a lamp; one page goes back to one block exactly once, then returns.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn object or scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, voice carries the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: Before pitching it, I tested the obvious alternative: just asking a chatbot. I gave plain Claude and ChatGPT the same idea, with a fake statistic planted in it. Both caught the fake number.

shot.visual_intent: Two comparison trays, each holding one idea page with a planted number; a terracotta check lands on the planted number in each tray.
shot.motion_claim: Two comparison trays, each holding one idea page with a planted number; a terracotta check lands on the planted number in each tray.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn object or scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, voice carries the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: But in three runs, plain Claude cited no sources, yet stated claims as facts. ChatGPT sourced just two paragraphs and left most claims unlabelled. You can't tell evidence from guesses.

shot.visual_intent: The same two trays: lines of claims fill each page in grey; source dots appear next to claims: none in the Claude tray; in the ChatGPT tray, dots beside just two paragraphs. A large ink 0 rises over the Claude tray.
shot.motion_claim: The same two trays: lines of claims fill each page in grey; source dots appear next to claims: none in the Claude tray; in the ChatGPT tray, dots beside just two paragraphs. A large ink 0 rises over the Claude tray.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn object or scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, voice carries the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: Paid tools exist too. DimeADozen's homepage promises hundred-page validation reports with hundreds of citations. I haven't bought one, so I can't judge them.

shot.visual_intent: A very thick stack of report pages builds up beside a price tag; a question mark draws over the stack.
shot.motion_claim: A very thick stack of report pages builds up beside a price tag; a question mark draws over the stack.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn object or scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, voice carries the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: Here's what will be different. Every claim will get a label, and code, not the model, will check each citation against the sources. The test scores will be public, including where it loses.

shot.visual_intent: Claim pages ride a conveyor through a checkpoint scanner beside the source binder; each page gets a tag, ink for sourced, grey for guess; one page fails the scan and is tagged guess.
shot.motion_claim: Claim pages ride a conveyor through a checkpoint scanner beside the source binder; each page gets a tag, ink for sourced, grey for guess; one page fails the scan and is tagged guess.

beats.narration_text: Who opens it? A hiring manager for AI product roles. In the first minute, they'll read the README, one real sample report, and the score table against plain chat.

shot.visual_intent: Three pages land on a desk in order, each with a one-word label; a cursor touches each in turn.
shot.motion_claim: Three pages land on a desk in order, each with a one-word label; a cursor touches each in turn.

beats.narration_text: What should it prove? That I can write prompt contracts, instructions plus a schema each agent's output must pass, and then measure whether they held. It won't prove I'm a machine learning engineer.

shot.visual_intent: A skill page and a gate: an agent's output parcel reaches the gate; the barrier lifts only after the parcel's shape matches the outline on the page.
shot.motion_claim: A skill page and a gate: an agent's output parcel reaches the gate; the barrier lifts only after the parcel's shape matches the outline on the page.

beats.narration_text: The evidence will be saved run logs, the score table, and a written list of where it failed.

shot.visual_intent: The evidence binder's cover opens; three tabbed sections slide out: logs, scores, failures.
shot.motion_claim: The evidence binder's cover opens; three tabbed sections slide out: logs, scores, failures.

beats.narration_text: What comes first: the risk agent and the evaluator, on one test idea, from the command line. You'll know it ran when a run log appears that passes the schema check.

shot.visual_intent: One idea parcel rides a short conveyor past one agent block and the review desk; a single log page drops out and a check draws on it.
shot.motion_claim: One idea parcel rides a short conveyor past one agent block and the review desk; a single log page drops out and a check draws on it.

beats.narration_text: What it will never do: give a percent chance of success, turning guesses into a probability. Live web search, accounts and forecasts are out too.

shot.visual_intent: A parcel stamped with a percent sign rides up to a permission gate; the barrier drops and blocks it; it slides off the stage.
shot.motion_claim: A parcel stamped with a percent sign rides up to a permission gate; the barrier drops and blocks it; it slides off the stage.

beats.narration_text: What could sink it? The evaluator rubber-stamps, the same model grading its own team. Chatbots already catch obvious fakes, so my test ideas will plant subtler flaws, like a price that contradicts the audience.

shot.visual_intent: A flawed page (a hairline terracotta crack) slides under an approval stamp; the stamp comes down and approves it anyway.
shot.motion_claim: A flawed page (a hairline terracotta crack) slides under an approval stamp; the stamp comes down and approves it anyway.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn object or scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, voice carries the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: So I'll count how many planted flaws it catches. If that number is low, I'll move checks out of the model and into plain code, and report the result either way.

shot.visual_intent: Sample cards with planted flaws slide into an experiment bench one by one; a tally of marks grows; a small dark code block docks next to the review desk.
shot.motion_claim: Sample cards with planted flaws slide into an experiment bench one by one; a tally of marks grows; a small dark code block docks next to the review desk.

beats.narration_text: Why this project? It's a mix. Requirements and challenging assumptions are years of my product work; WorkShip and SkillPort are on my GitHub. New to me: agent orchestration and evaluation design.

shot.visual_intent: Two shelves: the left one already holds three filled blocks; on the right shelf, three outlined empty slots draw in.
shot.motion_claim: Two shelves: the left one already holds three filled blocks; on the right shelf, three outlined empty slots draw in.

beats.narration_text: So, where it stands. What exists today: the idea, a blueprint I drafted with ChatGPT, and those chatbot tests. Everything else I will build with Claude Code, in two weeks.
